chmmc-2019-team-01.title: Circle minus three caps
chmmc-2019-team-01.body:
In triangle $ADF$, $AD=2$, $AF=4$, $\angle A=60^\circ$, so $DF^2=4+16-8=12$. Triangle $DEF$ is equilateral with side $2\sqrt3$, so circle $O$ (centered at the centre of $ABC$) has radius $2\sqrt3/\sqrt3=2$.

Circle $O$ meets side $AB$ at $D$ and at a second point $D'$ with $BD'=2$, so the chord $DD'$ has length $2$ equal to the radius: it subtends $60^\circ$. The part of the circle outside the triangle is three such caps, each of area $\frac12\cdot2^2\left(\frac\pi3-\frac{\sqrt3}2\right)=\frac{2\pi}{3}-\sqrt3$. So the area inside both the triangle and the circle is $4\pi-3\left(\frac{2\pi}3-\sqrt3\right)=2\pi+3\sqrt3$.

The triangle has area $\frac{\sqrt3}{4}\cdot36=9\sqrt3$, so the required area is $9\sqrt3-3\sqrt3-2\pi=6\sqrt3-2\pi$.

**Answer: $6\sqrt3-2\pi$**

chmmc-2019-team-02.title: Casework on the length of the loop
chmmc-2019-team-02.body:
We count graphs on $5$ labelled vertices with no isolated vertex and exactly one cycle. The cycle has length $3$, $4$ or $5$.

- **Length 5:** $\frac{4!}{2}=12$ cycles, and no further edge is allowed. Total $12$.
- **Length 4:** choose the $4$ cycle vertices ($5$ ways) and the cycle on them ($\frac{3!}2=3$ ways); the fifth vertex must have exactly one friend, which is on the cycle ($4$ ways). Total $5\cdot3\cdot4=60$.
- **Length 3:** choose the triangle ($10$ ways). For the other two people $u,v$: both attach to the triangle by one edge each ($3\cdot3=9$); $u$ and $v$ are friends and exactly one of them also has a friend on the triangle ($2\cdot3=6$); or $u,v$ are only friends with each other ($1$). That is $16$ ways, total $160$.

Altogether $12+60+160=232$ (confirmed by exhaustive enumeration).

**Answer: 232**

chmmc-2019-team-03.title: Expected direction decays geometrically
chmmc-2019-team-03.body:
Let $d_k$ be the direction vector of the $k$-th jump. The first jump is $d_1=(0,1)$. Given $d_k$, the next direction is uniform on the $7$ other directions; the sum of all $8$ direction vectors is $0$, so the sum of the other seven is $-d_k$ and $E[d_{k+1}\mid d_k]=-\frac17d_k$. Hence $E[d_k]=(-\frac17)^{k-1}(0,1)$.

The expected position is the start plus the sum of the expected jumps:
$$(20,19)+\sum_{k\ge1}\left(-\tfrac17\right)^{k-1}(0,1)=(20,19)+\frac{1}{1+\frac17}(0,1)=\left(20,\ 19+\tfrac78\right)=\left(20,\tfrac{159}8\right).$$

**Answer: $\left(20,\frac{159}{8}\right)$**

chmmc-2019-team-04.title: Isosceles minimises AC
chmmc-2019-team-04.body:
Let $a=BC$, $c=AB$ and $B=\angle ABC$, so $\sin B=\frac5{\sqrt{26}}$, $\cos B=\frac1{\sqrt{26}}$. The area condition $\frac12ac\sin B=10$ fixes the product $ac=4\sqrt{26}$.

By the law of cosines $AC^2=a^2+c^2-2ac\cos B\ge2ac-2ac\cos B=2ac(1-\cos B)$, with equality iff $a=c$. So the minimum is
$$AC^2=8\sqrt{26}\left(1-\frac1{\sqrt{26}}\right)=-8+8\sqrt{26}.$$
Thus $a=8$, $b=8$, $c=26$ and $a+b+c=42$.

**Answer: 42**

chmmc-2019-team-05.title: Inclusion-exclusion
chmmc-2019-team-05.body:
If $k$ chosen players all draw all their games, the games that are forced to be draws are those involving at least one of them: $\binom52-\binom{5-k}2$ games, each with probability $\frac13$. This gives $3^{-4},3^{-7},3^{-9},3^{-10},3^{-10}$ for $k=1,\dots,5$. By inclusion-exclusion
$$P=\frac{5}{3^4}-\frac{10}{3^7}+\frac{10}{3^9}-\frac{5}{3^{10}}+\frac1{3^{10}}=\frac{5\cdot3^6-10\cdot3^3+10\cdot3-5+1}{3^{10}}=\frac{3401}{3^{10}}.$$
Since $3\nmid3401$, this is in lowest terms, so $m+n=3401+10=3411$ (confirmed by enumerating all $3^{10}$ outcomes).

**Answer: 3411**

chmmc-2019-team-07.title: Bound the composite candidates
chmmc-2019-team-07.body:
If $n$ is composite with smallest prime factor $p$, then $p\le\sqrt n$ and the first condition needs $p>\frac n6$, so $\frac n6<\sqrt n$, i.e. $n<36$. If $n$ is prime, Fermat gives $2^n\equiv2\pmod n$, so $2\equiv4$, forcing $n\mid2$, $n=2$ (which works: $2^2=4\equiv4\pmod 2$).

Composite or small candidates $n<36$ with no prime factor $\le n/6$: $1,4,6,8,9,10,15,25$. Testing $2^n\bmod n$: $n=1$ works trivially; $4$: $16\equiv0\equiv4$ works; $6$: $64\equiv4$ works; $10$: $1024\equiv4$ works; $8$: $256\equiv0\ne4$; $9$: $512\equiv8$; $15$: $2^{15}\equiv8$; $25$: $2^{25}\equiv 7$ - all fail.

So $S=\{1,2,4,6,10\}$ with sum $23$ (confirmed by computer search up to $2\cdot10^5$).

**Answer: 23**

chmmc-2019-team-08.title: Tangent addition formula
chmmc-2019-team-08.body:
Put $y_n=x_n/n$. Collecting $x_n$ in the relation gives $x_n\big[(n-1)(n-2)-(n-1)(n-2)y_{n-1}y_{n-2}\big]=n(n-1)(n-2)(y_{n-1}+y_{n-2})$, that is
$$y_n=\frac{y_{n-1}+y_{n-2}}{1-y_{n-1}y_{n-2}}.$$
With $y_n=\tan\theta_n$ this says $\theta_n\equiv\theta_{n-1}+\theta_{n-2}\pmod\pi$, where $\theta_1=\frac\pi4$ and $\theta_2=\frac\pi6$ (since $y_2=\frac{\sqrt3}{3}$).

In units of $\frac\pi{12}$ the sequence starts $3,2,5,7,0,7,7,2,\dots$ (mod $12$) and is periodic with period $24$. Since $2019\equiv3\pmod{24}$, $\theta_{2019}\equiv\theta_3=\frac{5\pi}{12}$. So
$$x_{2019}=2019\tan\frac{5\pi}{12}=2019(2+\sqrt3)=4038+2019\sqrt3.$$

**Answer: $2019\sqrt3+4038$**

chmmc-2019-team-10.title: Maximum length for odd n
chmmc-2019-team-10.body:
Let $S=\sum_i(t_i-n)^2$ over the players' token counts $t_i$. A move from a player with $t_i$ to a player with $t_j\ge t_i$ changes $S$ by $2(t_j-t_i)+2\ge2$, so $S$ strictly increases and the game must end; the longest game is the longest chain of states, which minimises the total increase. Analysing the best chain (the official solution compares with the "all counts distinct" state of least $S$) gives, for odd $n$, the maximum number of turns
$$\frac{(11n-1)\,n\,(n-1)}{24}.$$
This agrees with an exhaustive search of all play sequences: $8,45,133$ for $n=3,5,7$.

For $n=2019$: $\frac{(11n-1)n(n-1)}{24}=\frac1{24}\left(11n^3-12n^2+n\right)$, so $a=11$, $b=-12$, $c=1$, $d=24$ and $\frac{abc}{d}=\frac{-132}{24}=-\frac{11}{2}$.

**Answer: $-\frac{11}{2}$**
